Homepage: a printed double page, typewritten mentions on the left, the logo on the right, a fold drawn in CSS
The idea

Studio Abîme is an independent Brussels communication lab that designs “sensory” identities, born from a dive beneath the visible. Its site is not a brochure but a printed board, an archive you leaf through: each page has its own staging, yet everything belongs to the same file.

The brand, logos, palette and the studio’s hypothesis — “to communicate is to link systems” — came from the client, who is also its own commissioner. I started from the territory they had set and translated it into a living interface: printed matter, archive paper, depth, investigation.
Homepage: two overlapping paper sheets fed automatically by the two latest journal articles
The lab: an orbit diagram presenting the method, “the substance comes before the form”
Experiences: client projects as the elements of a periodic table, empty cells standing for stories not yet heard
Project page: captioned figures, with three possible layouts per case
Contact: the enquiry form as a perforated paper file, with file number, numbered sections and a studio-only frame
Contact: an index of the studio’s vocabulary — Abyss, Archive, Workshop, Fragment, Seed, Dive
What I refused
No effect for effect’s sake: no gimmicks, no gratuitous 3D. Every movement has to guide, explain or give a rhythm.

No interaction that announces itself. The composition holds at rest; the reaction is discovered in passing. And nothing essential depends on hover, cursor or animation — the site reads by keyboard, with reduced motion and by touch.

No design settings in the back office. The CMS carries the content, layout is decided in code: the client keeps control of their words, not of the art direction, which protects the coherence over time.
How it is built

The site is built with Astro, using Vue only where interaction demands it (the journal explorer, the cart). Sanity carries the content, with visual editing in a split screen, and Shopify powers the shop. A small design system lets the graphic charter evolve without touching a single page.
Everything was designed to be multilingual, although it ships in French only. A page address is drawn from its title at first publication and then never moves.

Accessibility was part of the brief from the start: strong contrast, keyboard navigation and reduced motion are handled throughout. The direction follows one idea per page, with the content driving the composition.
Archive paper, sand, a warm light, a cold sky and the ink of a typewriter. Type is set in four voices — a mono for titles, a sans for subtitles, a narrow for text and an italic for annotations.
